extracted.intended_audience: students and readers studying Euclid's Elements / classical geometry (those learning geometric constructions and ratio-based reasoning)
extracted.subtask_description: Propositions and constructive criteria from Euclid (Book VI excerpt) about ratios of straight lines, parallelograms, and triangles, and how given ratios and given angles determine figures or enable finding other ratios. Includes methods to construct or find the required lines/figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXVI — sides determine corresponding side ratios in unequal-angled parallelograms
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two parallelograms have unequal, but given angles, and a given ratio to one another; if one side has to one side a given ratio, the other side has also a given ratio to the other side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation and construction: given equiangular/parallelogram ratio relations, one may construct straight lines so that corresponding side ratios are transferred. The text gives a constructive method: take a straight line H given in magnitude; make the ratio of H to K the same as the parallelogram AB to CD, then make the ratio of K to L the same as FD to EB; the ratio of AE to CF is then the same as H to L. The passage includes inversion and ex aequali steps to justify equality of ratios and shows how to find the ratio concretely by choosing auxiliary lines with the given ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXVII — equiangular parallelogram sides determine parallelogram ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the sides of two equiangular parallelograms have given ratios to one another; the parallelograms shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: given ratios AB:EF and BC:FG, construct straight lines K, L (starting from a given K) so that K:L equals AB:EF and L:K equals BC:FG, yielding lines K and M whose ratio equals the parallelogram AC to EG. The text explains taking a straight line K given in magnitude and making ratios to produce L and M; then by earlier propositions, parallelogram ratios correspond to ratios of these constructed straight lines. The passage explains how to 'find' the ratio when side ratios are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXVIII — unequal but given angles: side ratios determine parallelogram ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the sides of two parallelograms which have unequal, but given, angles, have given ratios to one another; the parallelograms shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: at a point B make an angle equal to the given angle of the second parallelogram and complete a parallelogram to relate sides; using given ratios of sides and angles one reduces the problem to earlier equiangular cases (prop. 67). The text gives a method using a given straight line MN and constructing angles equal to given ones, and then making segments NO:OP and MO:OP with the given side ratios so that AC:EG equals MO:OP. The explanation shows mapping from side ratios through similar triangles and equiangular parallelograms to deduce parallelogram ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: COR. 1 to PROP. 68 — triangles with two equal or given angles and given side ratios have given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles ABC, DEF have two equal angles, or two unequal but given angles, and if the ratios of the sides about these angles (e.g., AB:DE and BC:EF) be given; the triangles shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: complete parallelograms on the triangles' halves and use the parallelogram-ratio result (prop. 67) to deduce the ratio of the triangles. The corollary notes completing parallelograms BG, EH and that the triangles, being halves, inherit the given ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: COR. 2 to PROP. 68 — bases and cevians with given ratios determine triangle ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If the bases BC, EF of two triangles ABC, DEF have a given ratio to one another, and if also the straight lines AG, DH drawn to the bases from the opposite angles (either in equal angles or unequal but given angles) have a given ratio to one another: the triangles shall have a given ratio to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: draw parallels to transform the given cevians into parallelograms KC, LF; with given ratios of KB:LE and BC:EF and given relationships of angles, apply prop. 67 to the parallelograms to deduce triangle ratios. The corollary describes drawing BK, EL parallel to AG, DH and completing parallelograms KC, LF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXIX — parallelogram given in species when applied to side of given rectilineal figure with given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a parallelogram which has a given angle be applied to one side of a rectilineal figure given in species; if the figure have a given ratio to the parallelogram, the parallelogram is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof and construction: using parallels from vertices and producing lines to obtain given points H, K, deduce ratios KB:BC and KB:BA are given; show triangle BKE is given in species and hence EB:BA is given; because angle ABE is given, the parallelogram BF is given in species. Construction method: take a straight line LM given in magnitude, make angles equal to given ones and set LM:P equal to given figure-parallelogram ratios, then construct a parallelogram similar to BF (call it LS) via parallels and proportional reasoning. The section includes a full constructive recipe to find a parallelogram similar to the required one.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXX — given straight lines and given rectilineal figure/parallelogram ratios determine parallelogram in species
rubrics_metrics.description: IF two straight lines have a given ratio to one another, and upon one of them be described a rectilineal figure given in species, and upon the other a parallelogram having a given angle; if the figure have a given ratio to the parallelogram, the parallelogram is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: let AB:CD be given; on AB describe figure AEB and on CD parallelogram DF; because AB:CD given and similar figures/parallelograms are described upon them, ratios AG:FD etc. are given; reduce to case of prop. 69 (parallelogram applied to side of figure with given ratio) to find parallelogram FD in species. A step-by-step construction follows: choose H given, set ratios H:K same as figure:parallelogram, use earlier data to find K:L, then produce parallelogram MN similar to AG and show MN is similar to FD.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXI — means of proportional triplets inherit given ratios from extremes
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the extremes of three proportional straight lines have given ratios to the extremes of other three proportional straight lines; the means shall also have a given ratio to one another: and if one extreme has a given ratio to one extreme, and the mean to the mean; likewise the other extreme shall have to the other a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given A,B,C proportional and D,E,F proportional, with A:D and C:F given, then rectangle AC : DF is given; since square of B equals rectangle AC and square of E equals rectangle DF, square(B):square(E) is given; hence B:E is given. Conversely, if A:D and B:E are given then C:F is given by similar reasoning. The proposition includes the algebra-of-rectangles reasoning and a corollary extending to four proportionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXII — transferring 'given ratio to the straight line to which another has given ratio' across four proportionals
rubrics_metrics.description: IF four straight lines be proportionals; as the first is to the straight line to which the second has a given ratio, so is the third to a straight line to which the fourth has a given ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let A:B :: C:D. If B has given ratio to E, make D:F so that D:F equals B:E; then because proportions preserve multiplicative relations (ex æquali), A:E :: C:F. The proposition gives the construction: choose E (the line to which B has the given ratio) and construct F accordingly, establishing the analogous ratio for the third and fourth lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXIII — perturbation form for four proportionals with transferred given ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: IF four straight lines be proportionals; as the first is to the straight line to which the second has a given ratio, so is a straight line to which the third has a given ratio to the fourth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: given A:B :: C:D and given B:E, make F so that F:C :: B:E (i.e., F constructed to C as E to B); then by proportion perturbation (in proportione perturbata) deduce A:E :: F:D. The text explains making F to C as B is to E and invokes prior proportionality results to justify the equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXIV — ratio of excess of square (obtuse-angled triangle) to triangle
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a triangle has a given obtuse angle; the excess of the square of the side which subtends the obtuse angle, above the squares of the sides which contain it, shall have a given ratio to the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set-up: triangle ABC with given obtuse angle ABC; extend BA and draw AD perpendicular to BC. The excess (square of AC above squares of AB and BC) equals twice the rectangle DB·BC. Because triangle ABD is given in species, AD:DB is given; hence rectangle AD·BC to DB·BC ratio is given and twice that rectangle to triangle ABC is given (rectangle AD·BC is double the triangle). The proposition gives a concrete method for finding the ratio: take EF given, make angle EFG equal to ABC, draw EH perpendicular to FG; then the ratio of the excess to triangle ABC equals ratio of quadruple HF to HE. Detailed similar-triangle and rectangle-triangle relationships are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXV — ratio of deficit of square (acute-angled triangle) to triangle
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a triangle has a given acute angle, the space by which the square of the side subtending the acute angle is less than the squares of the sides which contain it, shall have a given ratio to the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to LXXIV: draw AD perpendicular to BC in triangle with given acute angle; the space (double the rectangle CB·BD) has a given ratio to the triangle. The argument uses that triangle ABD is given in species so BD:DA is given, hence rectangles and their ratios to the triangle are given. The proposition mentions the ratio may be found as in the preceding proposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEMMA — isosceles triangle base-segment square relation
rubrics_metrics.description: IF from the vertex A of an isosceles triangle ABC any straight line AD be drawn to the base BC, the square of the side AB is equal to the rectangle BD·DC of the segments of the base together with the square of AD; but if AD be drawn to the base produced, the square of AD is equal to the rectangle BD·DC together with the square of AB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs by bisecting the base and using right triangles: case 1 bisect base BC in E, join AE perpendicular to BC, deduce relations of squares and rectangles (referencing earlier Euclidean results). The lemma is used in subsequent propositions (e.g., LXXVI) to relate sums/differences of squares to rectangles of base segments and hence to triangle-area-type ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXVI — excess of square of equal-to-two-sides line above third side has given ratio to triangle
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a triangle have a given angle, the excess of the square of the straight line which is equal to the two sides that contain the given angle, above the square of the third side, shall have a given ratio to the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: produce BA and take AD equal to AC; join DC, produce to E, draw BE parallel to AC and AF perpendicular to DC. Using the lemma for isosceles triangle DBE, show rectangle DC·CE equals the excess of the square of BD (i.e., BA+AC) above square of BC; then show rectangle DC·CE has given ratio to triangle ABC via similar-triangle and rectangle-triangle relationships. The proposition also gives how to find the ratio concretely using an auxiliary line GH, constructing an isosceles-like configuration and comparing segments HK and GL to the triangle.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXVII — triangle determined in species by ratio of altitude to base
rubrics_metrics.description: IF the perpendicular drawn from a given angle of a triangle to the opposite side, or base, has a given ratio to the base, the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: if triangle is isosceles trivial; otherwise take EF given, describe segment of a circle EGF containing angle equal to given angle, bisect EF with GH, join EG, GF and adjust an angle FEL equal to the given base-angle, draw LM perpendicular to EF. Using similarity between ELF and BAG and ratios LM:EF = AD:BC one gets LM given, build parallelogram LMFK, deduce points and circumferences to construct triangle similar to ABC. Corollaries: (1) two triangles with same angle and same perpendicular:base ratio are similar; (2) if a cevian AR makes given ratio to BC in a given angle ARC then triangle is given in species; (3) more general statement about corresponding cevians with equal ratios and equal angles implying similarity. The text provides a full constructive method to produce a similar triangle.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. LXXVIII — triangle determined in species by given angle and given ratio of product of adjacent sides to square of base
rubrics_metrics.description: IF a triangle have one angle given, and if the ratio of the rectangle of the sides which contain the given angle to the square of the third side be given, the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: draw AD perpendicular to BC; rectangle AD·BC has given ratio to triangle ABC (being double the triangle); given rectangle BA·AC to BC^2 yields AD:BC ratio given. Then apply prop. 77 to construct triangle. Construction recipe: take EF given, make angle FEG equal to given angle, draw FH perpendicular to EG, form similar triangles ABK and EFH to connect rectangles and sides; set the given rectangle:base-square ratio equal to EF:FL, then find triangle OPQ by prop. 77 with the same perpendicular:base ratio. The proposition also gives the alternative path 'otherwise' wording for finding the triangle when AD:BC compares with MN:BC in a circumscribed segment.
